packs.title: Invention, Gardens and Sky
packs.promise: Discover San Jose through unusual architecture, art, living neighborhoods and mountain science.

q.t: A Street Scene in Four Shapes
q.s: Turn a commercial street scene into an original composition.
st: Choose a clear public position away from shop doors and dining tables.
Select four visible shapes from planting, street furniture or building edges.
Arrange them in a small original drawing without copying a logo or photographing shoppers.

q.t: A Garden in Its Own Season
q.s: Notice the garden as it is today.
st: Find a comfortable open path edge or seat.
Spend one quiet minute with a leaf, branch, flower or another detail that suits the season.
Write one observation without needing a particular bloom.

q.s: Look at an interactive exhibit as something someone designed.
st: Choose an available exhibit after checking its instructions.
Find two design features that help a visitor understand or use it.
Record what each feature seems to help with, distinguishing your interpretation from posted information.

packs.title: Street Frames, Small Stages
packs.promise: Find a creative district in its entrances, textures and small changes of pace.

q.s: Collect the small features that make a civic space work.
st: Choose an open public path away from event equipment.
Find a planted edge, a resting place and a change in paving that guides movement.
Make a three-symbol key explaining the practical job of each feature.

q.s: Find three textures without needing a particular mural.
st: Stop clear of doors and crossing approaches.
Find a smooth painted area, a textured surface and a small repeated joint on public-facing walls or fixtures.
Describe how one imaginary color would change across those three textures.

q.s: Collect three clues to an entrance at human scale.
st: Use a public-sidewalk view outside the arts space.
Find an entrance outline, a window or glazed area and a detail that distinguishes the front from the next building.
Make a three-part arrival card explaining what guides your eye toward the door.
